scope: Real-world-only long-term monitor v2 terminal state
summary: The v2 monitor exited cleanly after its only watched BWM process disappeared at the 12-hour GPU-wait timeout; it correctly did not launch the scientific postprocessor.
evidence: The monitor persisted 183 six-host capacity snapshots and two state-transition events.
Its final heartbeat records bwm-wipe20-seed42-real-world as failed and successor_started=false.
The detached monitor itself exited with code 0 after 26,417.63 seconds because all configured jobs were terminal.
lessons: Monitor process success and scientific job success must be reported separately.
Long-term monitor scope must include every active real-world waiter so one queue timeout does not end all campaign observation.
limitations: v2 watched only the BWM queue and did not include the DROID SVO calibration waiter.
next_actions: Start a v3 monitor for both the seven-day BWM waiter and DROID calibration waiter.
